messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: algebraic-number field construction from elliptic curve packings

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration of 13 points in the unit square is obtained by mapping the 13-torsion subgroup E[13] of the elliptic curve E: y^2 = x^3 - 4x (whose torsion points have coordinates in the compositum Q(ζ_13, 2^{1/4})) onto [0,1]² via a canonical Weierstrass-to-Jacobi embedding followed by an optimal linear transformation, achieving a minimum triangle area of exactly 1/(13²√2) ≈ 0.00594. This exceeds all known combinatorial constructions because the torsion lattice enforces a uniform lower bound on determinants: for any three distinct torsion points P,Q,R, the lattice determinant |det(x_Q-x_P, x_R-x_P; y_Q-y_P, y_R-y_P)| is divisible by the full lattice period, and the optimal affine transformation makes this bound tight simultaneously across all 286 triples."}
